result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a narrow, poorly maintained sidewalk on the left with significant debris and vegetation. The lack of marked crossings and physical buffers between the walkway and the roadway creates a high-risk environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Poor Sidewalk Condition
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is cracked, overgrown with weeds, and littered with debris, creating trip hazards and reducing usable width.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and midground sidewalk area

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs, forcing pedestrians to cross the street without designated protection.

hazards.name: Lack of Physical Buffer
hazards.description: Pedestrians are separated from moving traffic only by a painted bike lane, with no physical barriers, trees, or furniture to provide protection.
hazards.location_in_image: Edge of the left sidewalk adjacent to the roadway

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation and Widening
interventions.description: Repair the existing sidewalk surface to remove trip hazards and widen it to provide a clear, accessible walking path.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and pedestrian crossing signage to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at intersections or mid-block crossing points to shorten crossing distances and improve sight lines.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Green Buffer
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip with street trees between the sidewalk and the roadway to provide a physical and psychological buffer.

result.summary: The environment is dominated by a wide multi-lane roadway with minimal pedestrian infrastructure. While a sidewalk exists on the far side, there are no visible marked crossings, traffic signals, or traffic calming measures to support safe pedestrian movement across the street.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossing
hazards.description: There are no designated crossing points for pedestrians to reach the commercial destination from the residential area across the wide roadway.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the near side of the street may block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Marked Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a designated path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, which can also help slow traffic speeds.

result.summary: The street is a wide, car-oriented corridor with narrow sidewalks and no marked pedestrian crossings. The environment is characterized by industrial and commercial land uses with frequent driveway curb cuts and on-street parking that obstructs sightlines.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic without protection.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from large vehicles
hazards.description: A large tow truck and other parked vehicles on the right side block sightlines between pedestrians and moving traffic.

hazards.name: Frequent driveway curb cuts
hazards.description: Multiple vehicle access points cross the sidewalk on the right, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental-style crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility at crossing points.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing bike lane to a protected facility, which would also serve as a buffer for the sidewalk.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is severely compromised by a large accumulation of trash and debris that completely obstructs the sidewalk. This physical barrier, combined with poor pavement conditions, likely forces pedestrians into the roadway, significantly increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.

hazards.name: Trash and Debris
hazards.description: A large pile of garbage bags and loose litter blocks the entire width of the sidewalk, creating a physical barrier.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The sidewalk and curb area are cracked and crumbling, creating trip hazards.

interventions.title: Sanitation and Maintenance
interventions.description: Implement regular trash removal and street cleaning to ensure the sidewalk remains clear and accessible.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repair and level the sidewalk surface to provide a safe, ADA-compliant walking path.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians at night.
